written: P1-P7 2026-11-24, before any contact with an A7 III; P8-P10 2026-11-26, after the first tester's v1 run and before any v2 run
basis: a7m3_map FINDINGS.md M3-F002, F006, F011, F027, F030 (static analysis of the 4.04 update)
v1_outcome: first tester (macOS): P1-P3 held (054C:0C02 -> 054C:0336, authentication 4/4/4/6 on both devices, READ_HASP 88 bytes); P4 not reached: GET_FILE2 answered 0x10000004 with no data because the kit never sent Jiritsu MOUNT (M3-F030)

predictions.claim: The camera in Mass Storage mode answers PMCA-RE's start request and comes back as a service device with USB id 054C:0336 (the A7 IV's), or 054C:02A9.
predictions.source: M3-F006 (same Senser gadget); A7 IV CT1

predictions.claim: Authentication with PMCA-RE's public keys passes on the service device: three rounds answered 4, closing answer 6.
predictions.source: M3-F006: libsencore holds the A7 IV's three key blocks byte for byte

predictions.claim: /usr/share/pmbp/DeviceInfo.xml is 517 bytes, SHA-256 e44713178fad970870ead845c93abdfcf150c418de11b306da91f2d09d67c1b7 (the same file as the A7 IV's).
/usr/lib/libJiritsu.so, /usr/lib/libsencore.so, /usr/codec/vcd_firmware.bin and /system/av-cam.bin equal the 4.04 update's files (sizes and SHA-256 in expected_404.json).
/setting/DmmConfig.bin exists and equals update/0800_appli/setting/DmmConfig.bin. Low confidence: the installed copy may differ or be missing.
/proc/cpuinfo and /proc/iomem come back with no content (the file read sizes a file with stat, and /proc files report size 0).
predictions.source: libJiritsu.so calls __xstat; A7 IV CT1 /proc/cmdline came back empty

predictions.claim: Jiritsu MOUNT (0x4002, payload 00 00) succeeds: it creates /tmp/jiritsu and mounts /dev/nflasha6 there. Medium confidence: whether nflasha6 holds a valid FAT on a retail camera is unknown; if it does not, MOUNT fails and the first read again answers 0x10000004.
With the work area mounted, GET_FILE2 of ../../usr/share/pmbp/DeviceInfo.xml returns status 0 and the 517-byte file of P4.
The unmount form (00 01) answers without error and removes /tmp/jiritsu; the stop request then returns the camera to normal as in v1.
